parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by kinetic energy.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem: A cannon fires a shell vertically upwards. The shell leaves the cannon with a speed of $80\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and a kinetic energy of $480\text{ J}$. The shell then rises to a maximum height of $210\text{ m}$. The effect of air resistance is significant.
parts.text: Show that the mass of the shell is $0.15\text{ kg}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)1
parts.part_stem: For the movement of the shell from the cannon to its maximum height, calculate
parts.text: 1. the gain in gravitational potential energy,

parts.label: (b)(ii)2
parts.text: 2. the work done against air resistance.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the average force due to the air resistance acting on the shell as it moves from the cannon to its maximum height.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
The shell leaves the cannon at time $t = 0$ and reaches maximum height at time $t = T$.

On Fig. 2.1, sketch the variation with time $t$ of the velocity $v$ of the shell from time $t = 0$ to time $t = T$. Numerical values of $v$ and $t$ are not required.
{{figure:9702_w18_23_q02_figure_2_1}}
Fig. 2.1

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
The force due to the air resistance is a vector quantity.

Compare the force due to the air resistance acting on the shell as it rises with the force due to the air resistance as it falls.
